data.name: Farrad
data.gender_notes: Farrad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Farrad is derived from the Arabic word 'farada' which means 'to decide' or 'to determine'. It is a powerful name for a boy that signifies strength, resolve and the ability to make decisive choices. It also implies wisdom and intelligence. The name Farrad carries the meaning “Determined, Decisive, Resolute” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Farrad usually hope their child will grow to embody determined, decisive, resolute and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies the strength and determination of the divine will.
data.etymology: Farrad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Determined, Decisive, Resolute.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Farrad total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.context: Farrad was a chief of the Banu Hilal tribe, who invaded Egypt in 1168 AD. Farrad led the camel corps of the invading army and was a significant military commander during the conquest.

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi, The History of Damascus and the Principal Events of the Islamic World, translated by H.A.R. Gibb, C.F. Beckingham. Oxford University Press, 1969.
historical_references.context: Farrad was a chief of the Banu Sa'id tribe, who were part of the Mamluk army that defended Egypt against the invasion by Timur (Tamerlane) in 1401 AD. Farrad played a crucial role in the defense of the city of Damietta and was later appointed as the governor of the city.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Farrad, which originated from the Islamic financial concept of 'Fard' (an obligation or a debt), has gained significant traction in modern contexts. It is particularly relevant in the Islamic finance sector, where Farrad refers to the mandatory debt repayment to be made in accordance with Sharia law. Moreover, with the ongoing digital transformation, Farrad has found new avenues through mobile wallets, online banking apps, and social media platforms. These digital tools enable seamless and efficient debt management, making Farrad a vital concept in the era of technology-driven financial services. The trend towards e-commerce also plays a role, as more businesses adopt digital platforms for transactions, further expanding the reach and relevance of Farrad.
